section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Return, O Israel, until Hashem your G-d" and questions the precise wording and the mention of both Divine names.
section.t: "Return, O Israel, until Hashem your G-d,"
And the precise point in this is known, that it says "until Hashem your G-d,"
for ostensibly it should have said "to Hashem your G-d."
And also, what is mentioned here, the two names, Hashem and Elokim.
Also, it requires explanation, what the verse continues, "for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
for this, that repentance
("Return")
is for sin and iniquity, is understood by itself,
what does the verse innovate with "for you have stumbled in your iniquity"?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of Divine service, "turn from evil" and "do good," correspond to the names Elokim and Hashem, which relate to the immanent and transcendent lights respectively, and details the nature of creation from these two lights.
section.t: And the explanation is,
that in the service of man there are two matters in general.
"Turn from evil and do good."
And it is known
that the service of "turn from evil" pertains
(primarily)
to the name Elokim,
and the service of "do good" to the name Hashem.
And the explanation is,
as it is brought in the Shulchan Aruch,
that when one mentions the name Hashem, one must intend that He is the One who was, is, and will be,
and when one mentions the name Elokim, one must intend that He is the Mighty and Strong One, who has the ability in the upper realms and the lower realms.
And from the distinction between these two matters is,
that this One who has the ability in the upper realms and the lower realms is in the G-dliness that is relative to the worlds,
which in general is "He fills all worlds,"
and this One who is the One who was, is, and will be as one
is in the G-dliness that is above the worlds,
"He encompasses all worlds."
And the explanation is,
that the definition of a world is place and time,
for so it is also in the spiritual worlds, which are defined by the definition of place and time,
except that the place and time within them are a spiritual place and time.
And since the light that fills is a light relative to the worlds,
it is understood,
that also in the light that fills there is something analogous to place and time,
[And as is known
that in the light of the line,
which in general is the light that fills,
there exist the matters of above and below
(place)
and precedence and posteriority
(time)],
which is the root of place and time in the worlds.
And this that Hashem is the One who was, is, and will be as one, above the division of time,
is,
because Hashem is the light that is above the worlds.
However, even so,
from this that we say that Hashem is the One who was, is, and will be as one
[for "was, is, and will be" are matters of time,
except that it is above division],
it is understood,
that also Hashem relates to time
(worlds),
for this is also what Hashem is a term meaning "He brings into being,"
for the bringing into being of all the worlds is from the name Hashem.
Except that the worlds as they are brought into being from the name Hashem are not so limited,
therefore,
the past, present, and future are as one.
And this is that Hashem and Elokim are "He encompasses all worlds" and "He fills all worlds,"
for the bringing into being from the light that fills,
since it is relative to the worlds and a source for them,
is in a manner of enclothing.
Therefore, the worlds that are brought into being from it have existence,
for the matter of enclothing is that it enclothes itself to bring the worlds into being,
and the bringing into being from the encompassing light,
since the worlds have no value relative to it,
is in a manner of automatically,
analogous to an action that comes from the will
(for will is a parable for the encompassing),
for the will is only a cause for the action and does not enclothe itself within it.
Therefore, the worlds that are brought into being from the encompassing light are not in the category of existence,
for just as the will itself is not an existence and is only a revelation of the essence
[and analogous to the will in the soul of man, which is only an inclination and extension of the soul],
so too is it regarding the bringing into being from the will,
that its matter is
(not that worlds are brought into being,
but rather)
that through the bringing into being, the will is completed.
And this is the connection of the encompassing light and the light that fills to the names Hashem and Elokim,
for the light that fills is called by the name Elokim, from the word meaning "power,"
for it is analogous to a power, whose matter is to act.
Except that since the existence of the worlds is through this, that the G-dly power brings them into being every moment from nothing to something,
therefore the intention in the name Elokim is "who has the ability in the upper realms and the lower realms,"
that the dominion and rulership of Him
(Elokim from the word meaning "authority")
over the upper realms and the lower realms is also after they have been brought into being,
and the rulership over them is also regarding the essence of their existence
(whether to bring them into being or not).
And the encompassing light is called by the name Hashem,
the One who was, is, and will be as one,
for since the bringing into being from the encompassing light, its matter is that through the bringing into being, the will is completed,
therefore there is no distinction in this between past, present, and future,
the One who was, is, and will be as one.
